title: Rough to XHV: The Full Vacuum Pressure Ladder
h1: Vacuum pressure ranges — rough, medium, high, UHV and XHV
description: Vacuum spans 15 decades from 1 atm to below 10⁻¹² torr. Each decade needs a different pump. Here is the complete map with torr, mbar and Pa side by side.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: 1 atm → 760 torr → 101325 Pa. UHV → 10⁻¹⁰ torr → 10⁻⁸ Pa. Ninteen decades of pressure, five pump families, one messy vocabulary.
body: Vacuum work is stratified by decade of pressure. Each stratum runs on a different pump technology, different gauge, and different chamber material. Convert between them fluently or misspec the pump by three orders of magnitude.

> Low vacuum (rough): 1013 – 1 mbar (760 – 0.75 torr). Rotary vane, scroll, diaphragm pumps.
> Medium vacuum: 1 – 10⁻³ mbar. Roots blowers, oil diffusion.
> High vacuum (HV): 10⁻³ – 10⁻⁸ mbar. Turbomolecular pumps.
> Ultra-high vacuum (UHV): 10⁻⁸ – 10⁻¹² mbar. Ion, cryo, titanium sublimation pumps.
> Extreme high vacuum (XHV): below 10⁻¹² mbar. Combined pumping and baking.

At 1 mbar the mean free path is a few centimetres; molecules still collide constantly. At 10⁻⁶ mbar it is 50 m; at 10⁻¹⁰ mbar it takes an hour for a monolayer to deposit. Surface science, semiconductor deposition, particle accelerators live in UHV/XHV — everyday coatings do not.
US semiconductor: torr and millitorr. European semiconductor and physics: mbar. SI-strict labs: Pa. Charts routinely list all three.
Rough → 1 mbar. HV → turbo. UHV → ion+cryo+bakeout. Wrong pump for the decade means you never reach base pressure.

faqs.a: The lowest pressure a chamber reaches with pumps running and no gas load. Set by outgassing rate divided by pumping speed.
Water desorbs from stainless steel walls for weeks at room temperature. A 150–250 °C bakeout drives it off in hours, dropping base pressure two decades.
